candidates.name: edgartools
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library covering 20+ SEC filing types back to 1994: parses 13F institutional-holdings/hedge-fund portfolios, Form 4 insider transactions into DataFrames, XBRL-standardized income/balance/cash-flow statements, 10-K/10-Q/8-K/proxy. No data committed to the repo; pulls live from EDGAR on demand. MIT license, 2.7k stars, 4,388 commits, active (updated 2026).
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose, well-maintained method to pull ABNB's own 13F institutional-ownership history (concentration/turnover of holders) and any Form 4 insider transactions for ABNB officers/directors -- directly addresses gap #15 (company-structure signals: 13F parsers, concentration history, SEC EDGAR tooling).

candidates.name: ishares
candidates.what_it_holds: Scrapes ETF holdings histories directly from iShares.com: security-level ticker, name, sector, asset class, market value, weight, shares outstanding, price, per ETF per reporting date, back to 2006, monthly snapshots. CSV output, optional AWS S3 + Athena integration, master ETF index at ./ishares/data/ishares-etf-index.csv. 38 stars, 11 forks, 42 commits, updated 2026-07-14.
candidates.why_useful: A working, long-history (2006-) method to pull ETF-level holdings/weights over time -- useful for tracking passive-fund exposure to ABNB or travel/consumer-discretionary ETFs (basket concentration, flow-implied ownership changes) as an institutional-positioning proxy; addresses gap #15 and adjacent to markets/positioning gaps.
candidates.size_hint: scraper + index CSV, no bulk pre-pulled history committed

candidates.name: 13f-portfolio-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Reconstructs institutional portfolios from raw SEC EDGAR 13F filings: idempotent ingestion, per-filing value-unit verification, multi-strategy CUSIP resolution (claims 99.68% resolved by value), amendment-aware quarter-over-quarter diffs, Streamlit dashboard where every number traces back to its EDGAR accession number. Updated 2026-09-08 (very recent).
candidates.why_useful: More rigorous 13F pipeline than the toy scrapers -- CUSIP resolution and amendment handling matter for building a clean institutional-ownership-concentration time series for ABNB or its holders/comps; addresses gap #15.

candidates.name: alphasmo-tools
candidates.what_it_holds: CLI + MCP server for SEC EDGAR 13F filings, insider trading (Form 4), and "Smart Money convergence signals" (cross-referencing institutional and insider activity). MIT license, 2 stars, updated 2026-08-12.
candidates.why_useful: Combines 13F and Form 4 access with a convergence-signal layer already built; could be repurposed to watch ABNB institutional/insider activity around print dates without building the plumbing.

candidates.name: sec-form4-insider-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Scrapes and structures SEC Form 4 insider-trading filings into a queryable SQLite database. 1 star, Python.
candidates.why_useful: A structured (SQLite, queryable) rather than ad-hoc Form 4 pipeline -- lower-friction than scraping EDGAR by hand for ABNB officer/director transaction history around guide dates.
candidates.size_hint: SQLite DB schema + scraper, no pre-populated data

candidates.name: secform4
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scripts (sec_filings.py, sec_analyst.py, all_companies.py) to track all SEC Form 4 insider-trading filings across companies and "investigate insider sentiment quicker". 8 commits, no license specified.
candidates.why_useful: Cross-company Form 4 puller could be pointed at ABNB and peers (BKNG, EXPE) to build an insider-sentiment time series; addresses gap #15.

candidates.name: sec-web-scraper-13f
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper (Requests/lxml/BeautifulSoup) that pulls a fund's 13F filings from SEC EDGAR by CIK and outputs a TSV of holdings. 48 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Simple, moderately popular 13F-by-CIK puller; a fallback method if edgartools is overkill. Addresses gap #15.

candidates.name: 13f-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scrapes/parses/normalizes SEC 13F filings via CLI and Python API; lookup by fund name, CIK, or CSV upload; outputs CSV (fund name, CIK, filing period, first-time-filer flag, holdings count) and detailed holdings CSV/JSONL. First-time-filer detection, holdings-count filtering, REST API, rate-limited SEC compliance, response caching. MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: More feature-complete 13F puller than most (first-time-filer detection is useful for spotting new institutional entrants into ABNB); addresses gap #15.

candidates.name: finra_short_interest_fetcher
candidates.what_it_holds: Fetches FINRA short-interest data. No stars, updated 2023-03-18, no license listed.
candidates.why_useful: A working puller for FINRA's bi-monthly short-interest-by-security releases, which could extend our existing short-interest holding with a maintained script (or verify our vintages against a second source). Addresses part of gap #15/positioning tracking.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold ABNB short interest; this is a generic fetcher, not new coverage

candidates.name: si-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: FINRA short-interest dashboard covering 40 sector/industry themes, sector-sentiment aggregation, and a "rising shorts" screener. Updated 2026-08-17, no license listed.
candidates.why_useful: Sector-level (travel/consumer discretionary) short-interest aggregation could contextualize ABNB's own short-interest trend against its peer/sector cohort.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold ABNB short interest

candidates.name: 13f_info_get_fund_holdings
candidates.what_it_holds: BeautifulSoup scraper of 13f.info for historical holdings of specific fund managers (Berkshire Hathaway, Bridgewater, Pershing Square, etc.). CC0-1.0 license (public domain), 1 star, updated 2025-03-03.
candidates.why_useful: A route to specific well-known funds' historical ABNB position sizes (if held) via 13f.info rather than raw EDGAR XML; CC0 license means output is freely reusable.

candidates.name: swift-edgar
candidates.what_it_holds: Native Swift, zero-dependency, async/await client for SEC EDGAR covering 13F filings, XBRL financials, insider trading (Form 4), fund holdings, and company search. MIT license, 1 star, updated 2026-07-12.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative-language (Swift) EDGAR client bundling 13F + Form 4 + fund holdings in one API; low practical value for a Python-based pipeline but confirms the method space is active and well-covered.

candidates.name: trade-copier-13f
candidates.what_it_holds: Pulls a chosen filer's SEC EDGAR 13F holdings, diffs consecutive quarters, and dry-runs proportional "mirror" trades on Alpaca paper trading (risk-gated); explicitly notes the 45-day disclosure lag and includes an honest backtest vs SPY. Updated 2026-09-03.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates the quarter-over-quarter diff mechanics for a single filer's 13F holdings (useful pattern for building an ABNB-holder concentration/turnover series) and is refreshingly explicit about the reporting lag, which matters for point-in-time discipline.

candidates.name: thirteen-f-scrape
candidates.what_it_holds: SEC EDGAR 13F filings scraper plus a Dagster/DuckDB/Evidence data-pipeline and dashboard stack. Updated 2026-04-09, no license listed.
candidates.why_useful: A more production-grade (orchestrated, DuckDB-backed) 13F pipeline than the ad-hoc scrapers -- fits our DuckDB-centric workflow if we wanted to stand up an ongoing 13F pull rather than a one-off script.

candidates.name: insidercluster
candidates.what_it_holds: Free SEC Form 4 cluster-buy detector: flags Code-P (open-market purchase) filings where 3+ insiders buy within a 14-day window. Updated 2026-06-03.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made cluster-buy signal detector on Form 4 data that could be pointed at ABNB (and BKNG/EXPE/hotel peers) to flag coordinated insider buying around guide dates.

candidates.name: sec_13f_filing_parser
candidates.what_it_holds: Parses 13F filing header and position info from raw SEC XML/text into structured records. 2 stars, last updated 2020-03-16.
candidates.why_useful: Older but simple, focused 13F header+position parser -- useful as a lightweight reference implementation if edgartools proves too heavy.

notes: This session's shared WebSearch budget (200/200) was already exhausted before any of my four WebSearch calls returned results, so I fell back per instructions. DuckDuckGo HTML (html.duckduckgo.com/html/) served only a CAPTCHA challenge page to WebFetch and returned zero usable results across all four attempts -- dead end for this modality going forward. Bing search-results pages rendered but WebFetch's summarizer described only the visible teaser snippets, not real GitHub links -- also low-yield. github.com/search?q=...&type=repositories worked well via WebFetch when it wasn't 429'd, but hit HTTP 429 roughly half the time (no clear cooldown pattern within the session). gh search repos via the Bash tool (GitHub REST search API) was the most reliable channel once its own 403 rate-limit windows passed (hit the shared 5,000/hr cross-agent budget twice, at which point I stopped rather than sleep/retry-loop). Overall finding: this theme is a crowded, low-differentiation space on GitHub -- dozens of ABNB-agnostic 13F/Form-4/short-interest scrapers exist, nearly all thin wrappers around SEC EDGAR or FINRA with no committed historical data and mostly 0-2 stars; edgartools and talsan/ishares stand out as the two genuinely substantial, maintained, general-purpose tools. I found no repo that holds ABNB-specific institutional-ownership, insider-transaction, or short-interest history already assembled, nor any pre-2023 archived short-interest or 13F dataset -- everything here is a pull-method (data_kind='acquisition_method'), which matches gap #15's framing (parsers/tooling, not finished datasets). Worth a future scout: ETF-flow datasets specifically for XLY/consumer-discretionary or travel-themed ETFs (e.g. JETS, AWAY) as an institutional-positioning proxy for the travel trade broadly -- I did not find a dedicated repo for that narrower angle and ran out of budget before searching it directly.
